text:
maria: quick heads-up — perf probe from prod-canary shows some unexpected prefix-cache behavior that looks like cross-tenant collisions. posting a short dump + thoughts.

infra-bot: deployment canary/rv3: cache_prefix_probe: tenant=tenant-A model=redwood-7b prefix_hash=0x9f3a -> store
infra-bot: cache_get: tenant=tenant-B model=redwood-7b prefix_hash=0x9f3a -> HIT (returned tenant-A response)

maria: exact sequence above — two different tenants ended up hitting the same cache entry. seems rare but reproducible on r2 nodes when sequence-lengths are short and we apply the current prefix normalization (lowercasing + whitespace collapse).

lucy: thanks. did we confirm it's a key-collision (same final cache key) and not a routing mixup? logs show identical cache_key values, yes?

maria: yes, logs show identical `cache_key` (base64) and identical `key_tag` in the runtime. routing metadata indicates correct tenant ownership, which suggests cache key derivation is not mixing tenant scope properly.

ben: initial thought: we intentionally stripped tenant id from derivation to increase cross-tenant hit rate (higher cache reuse). tradeoff was performance. but this leaks responses across tenants — unacceptable.

ajay: agreed — even if contents are low-sensitivity, this is a security/PII risk. we need an immediate mitigation + longer-term design. short fix: reintroduce tenant-scope into the cache key (cheap) and audit for collisions.

maria: proposal (short-term): key derivation = HMAC_SHA256(tenant_hmac_salt, model + '|' + model_version + '|' + prefix_digest) and include a small keyspace version byte. Also mark entries with encrypted metadata so runtime refuses to serve if tenant mismatch.

lucy: code sketch:
```python
# tenant_salt is per-tenant secret pulled from KMS at startup
prefix_digest = sha256(prefix_bytes)
raw = model.encode() + b"|" + model_version.encode() + b"|" + prefix_digest
cache_key = base64url(hmac_sha256(tenant_salt, raw)[:16])
# store: ciphertext = AESGCM.encrypt(dek_for_tenant, response_bytes, associated_data=tenant_id)
```

ben: perf notes: doing HMAC + AES encrypt per store will add CPU on cold writes and decrypt on reads. rough numbers from microbench: HMAC_SHA256 ~ 0.6us/op on our cpu, AESGCM ~ 1.2us/op, but overhead in our runtime adds ~0.8ms median for cold path due to encoder/decoding and python->rust boundaries. Expect ~3-8% latency increase at low loads; batching should amortize.

maria: mitigations: lazy-decrypt on read (only decrypt when returning to network), keep header metadata unencrypted (tenant id, model) so routing still works, and use DEK caching to avoid KMS roundtrips.

lucy: warmup strategy to reduce cold penalty: when a model rollout or shard spin-up happens, run tenant-aware warmers that prepopulate prefix cache for the high-volume tenants. i.e. warmup workers take a small sample of recent prefixes per tenant and seed caches encrypted with the tenant DEK.

ajay: audit requirements: log every decrypt attempt (who requested DEK, service principal), emit an event for any key mismatch (cache entry tenant != request tenant), and run weekly collision-scan job that looks for identical cache_key values across tenants historically. retention + access controls applied.

security-bot: policy note: creating per-tenant DEKs requires a small KMS ops change (grant runtime the ability to unwrap tenant DEKs) and update to our access-review playbook.

maria: rollout plan:
- step 1: implement tenant-scoped HMAC key derivation + store tenant_id metadata (no encryption) behind a feature flag
- step 2: canary 5% traffic for 24h, measure collisions (should go down to 0), monitor p95 latency and CPU
- step 3: enable AEAD encryption of cache values + DEK caching in runtime (another canary)
- step 4: enable warmup workers in dedicated mode for top N tenants
- fallback: control-plane flag to revert to old behavior if perf regressions beyond threshold

ben: metrics to track:
- cache_collision_count (per-minute)
- cache_hit_rate_by_tenant
- cold_write_latency_ms
- decrypt_ops/sec and KMS unwrap/sec
- audit: decrypt_log_count

lucy: for the weekly collision-scan harness, I can throw together a quick Spark job to scan our cache metadata table and surface any cache_key used by >1 tenant in the last 30d. will add regression tests for salted keys and cross-tenant scan.

ajay: action items:
- @maria implement HMAC derivation PR + unit tests (ETA 2d)
- @ben add metrics and an alert if collisions > 0 after rollout (urgent)
- @lucy build collision-scan job and warmup worker prototype (ETA 1w)
- security: I'll update KMS grants + run an access review before AEAD rollout

maria: ok i'll open the PR and link here. low-priority: consider opt-in sharing mode for tenants that want to share common prefixes (explicit contract) — but default must be isolated.

ben: :thumbsup: appreciate the clear plan. add a canary dashboard.

lucy: :eyes: adding unit perf tests to CI to catch regressions in HMAC+AEAD path.

maria: thanks all — PR soon, will ping once canary is live.
